full_list.title_en: In the age of big data and AI: do we still need chemical bonds?
full_list.title_zh: 在大数据和人工智能时代：我们还需要化学键吗？
full_list.abstract: arXiv:2611.00228v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Chemical bonding is the language through which chemistry rationalizes materials structure, stability, properties, and reactivity. Meanwhile, modern deep-learning models achieve remarkable predictive performance using representations based largely on compositional and structural information, raising the question of whether explicit bonding concepts remain necessary. In this work, we argue that artificial intelligence does not render chemical bonding obsolete but provides a new framework for evaluating and refining bonding concepts. We show that, through linear probing, Allegro and MACE embeddings recover bonding descriptors with (R² > 0.95), indicating that bonding emerges naturally from Allegro's and MACE's latent spaces. We also show that bonding descriptors provide information beyond bond distance in our electronic-structure-featurized MEGNet (ESF-MEGNet) model, reducing prediction error for properties including bulk and shear moduli by 15%. We discuss implications for interpretable machine learning, synthesizability prediction, and generative materials design, and suggest joint-embedding approaches for learning more general bonding representations. More broadly, we propose that chemical bonding can be understood as a learnable representation of electronic structure. From this perspective, different bonding models represent alternative compressions of the underlying electronic information and can be evaluated through their predictive power, dimensionality, and complexity. The age of machine learning shifts the focus from whether a bonding model is physically motivated to whether it captures the information required to explain and predict materials behavior. If a materials genome exists, it should be encodable through a representation of chemical bonding. If no bonding representation can capture this information, our understanding of the chemical bond may require revision.
full_list.abstract_zh: 化学键合是化学使材料结构、稳定性、性能和反应性合理化的语言。与此同时，现代深度学习模型使用主要基于组成和结构信息的表示来实现显着的预测性能，这就提出了显式键合概念是否仍有必要的问题。在这项工作中，我们认为人工智能并没有使化学键合过时，而是为评估和完善键合概念提供了一个新的框架。我们表明，通过线性探测， Allegro和MACE嵌入恢复与（ R ² > 0.95 ）的键合描述符，表明键合自然地从Allegro和MACE的潜在空间中出现。
full_list.abstract_zh_full: 化学键合是化学使材料结构、稳定性、性能和反应性合理化的语言。与此同时，现代深度学习模型使用主要基于组成和结构信息的表示来实现显着的预测性能，这就提出了显式键合概念是否仍有必要的问题。在这项工作中，我们认为人工智能并没有使化学键合过时，而是为评估和完善键合概念提供了一个新的框架。我们表明，通过线性探测， Allegro和MACE嵌入恢复与（ R ² > 0.95 ）的键合描述符，表明键合自然地从Allegro和MACE的潜在空间中出现。我们还表明，在我们的电子结构特征化MEGNet （ ESF-MEGNet ）模型中，键合描述符提供了超出键合距离的信息，将包括体积和剪切模量在内的属性的预测误差降低了15%。我们讨论了可解释机器学习、可合成性预测和生成材料设计的含义，并提出了学习更一般键合表示的联合嵌入方法。更广泛地说，我们提出化学键可以理解为电子结构的可学习表示。从这个角度来看，不同的键合模型代表了底层电子信息的替代压缩，可以通过其预测能力、维度和复杂性进行评估。机器学习的时代将重点从键合模型是否具有物理动机转移到它是否捕获解释和预测材料行为所需的信息。如果材料基因组存在，它应该可以通过化学键的表示进行编码。如果没有键合表示可以捕获这些信息，我们对化学键的理解可能需要修改。

full_list.method_point: 方法上，摘要目前只能确认：论文题目和摘要中可确认的方法。需要回到原文核对数据来源、标签定义、模型架构、物理约束和验证集，不能把题名直接等同于可迁移算法。若要接入团队的 ML 势或 Hamiltonian 流程，应先确认它是否同时学习能量、力、应力、自旋、极化或电子结构，以及是否报告跨材料/跨温度外推。还需核对原文的训练数据规模、损失函数、边界条件和误差分解，才能判断其是否适合团队的材料模拟任务。
full_list.related_work: 与团队方向的可能连接在于：晶体结构、功能材料和结构—性质关系。团队已有机器学习势、第一性原理、有效 Hamiltonian、缺陷计算、电子—声子耦合和有限温度动力学基础，但该文是否提供可复用数据或物理量仍需查证。若研究对象属于机器人、量子信息或电网等非材料场景，关联主要是物理约束学习、少样本建模或不确定性评估，而不是直接迁移材料机制。这种联系应通过同一材料体系上的独立基准和跨分布测试确认，不能仅凭方法名称或期刊来源下结论。
full_list.implication: 对《在大数据和人工智能时代：我们还需要化学键吗？》的启示是先做可证伪的对接：从一个已有材料体系和小规模 DFT 基准开始，明确输入、目标、基线和外推测试，再决定是否接入铁电/磁性、缺陷或载流子动力学工作。具体可先把该文的表示或损失函数在 HfO₂、二维滑移铁电、CrI₃/CrSBr、SiC/GaN 缺陷或卤化物钙钛矿上做小规模复现；若没有直接交叉，应保留为方法参考而非强行迁移。第一步可以选取团队已有的 HfO₂、二维磁体、半导体缺陷或钙钛矿数据做小样本试验，再决定是否扩大到生产级计算。

full_list.title_en: PaddleMaterials: An End-to-End Deep Learning Toolkit for Materials Science
full_list.title_zh: 文献研究：PaddleMaterials: An End-to-End Deep Learning Toolkit for Materials Science
full_list.abstract: arXiv:2611.03154v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Machine learning supports materials design, atomistic simulation and experimental characterization, yet models and workflows remain fragmented. We present PaddleMaterials, an open-source framework integrating heterogeneous materials-learning tasks while preserving task-specific representations and scientific semantics. It unifies data processing, training, evaluation, pretrained-model management and workflows across six task classes: property prediction, structure generation, machine-learning interatomic potentials, electronic-structure fields, spectrum elucidation and microscopy image processing. Task interfaces record physical quantities, units, aggregation conventions and references, making cross-task composition verifiable. A shared compiler backend enables switching from dynamic-graph to compiled execution through one setting, using graph optimization, operator fusion and hardware-targeted code generation without changing model definitions. Across 65 model instances in 11 groups, compiled execution accelerated every instance in eight groups, with group median speedups of 11%-224% and group maximum speedups of 11%-336%. Case studies on LiMnO2 and toluene link structure generation or spectrum elucidation, interatomic-potential relaxation, property prediction and electron-density prediction, using same-geometry density functional theory (DFT) calculations as references. For LiMnO2, predicted formation energies for generated and relaxed structures differed from same-geometry PBE+U references by at most 7 meV per atom, while the computational cost of model steps was less than one-twentieth of a DFT single-point calculation. PaddleMaterials extends unified materials workflows beyond conventional property, potential and structure-generation tasks while supporting verifiable cross-task operations and compiled execution.

full_list.method_point: 方法上，这篇工作可归入HfO₂ 铁电、二维滑移铁电、极化翻转、畴壁和疲劳/缺陷问题。从摘要能确认的线索包括：密度泛函理论和电子结构计算，以及缺陷、畴壁、成核和开关动力学, 晶体结构、功能材料和结构—性质关系对应的结构或物理量。若迁移到团队流程，应采用“把电场、极化、应变、氧空位和局域结构序参一起纳入轨迹数据；比较均匀翻转、局域成核和畴壁传播，并用 DFT/有效 Hamiltonian 对关键路径复核”的分层验证，而不是只比较单点能量或单一回归误差。还需核对原文的训练数据规模、损失函数、边界条件和误差分解，才能判断其是否适合团队的材料模拟任务。
full_list.related_work: 它与五位研究人员已有工作的直接连接是：HfO₂ 铁电、二维滑移铁电、极化翻转、畴壁和疲劳/缺陷问题已经出现在团队的方向画像中，可对应到HfO₂、Hf₀.₅Zr₀.₅O₂、二维范德华铁电、钙钛矿氧化物。与传统只做 0 K formation energy/静态势垒的工作相比，这里更应关注缺陷、畴壁、成核和开关动力学, 晶体结构、功能材料和结构—性质关系在温度、缺陷、应变或外场下的变化；摘要没有给出的模型细节不作延伸判断。这种联系应通过同一材料体系上的独立基准和跨分布测试确认，不能仅凭方法名称或期刊来源下结论。
full_list.implication: 对当前研究最具体的启示不是泛泛地“使用 ML”，而是把该文的HfO₂ 铁电、二维滑移铁电、极化翻转、畴壁和疲劳/缺陷问题嵌入现有材料模拟链：先在HfO₂、Hf₀.₅Zr₀.₅O₂、二维范德华铁电、钙钛矿氧化物中选择一个已有 DFT 数据基础的体系，按“把电场、极化、应变、氧空位和局域结构序参一起纳入轨迹数据；比较均匀翻转、局域成核和畴壁传播，并用 DFT/有效 Hamiltonian 对关键路径复核”补充训练/验证集，再比较《PaddleMaterials: An End-to-End Deep Learning Toolkit for Materials Science》对应模型对相稳定、极化/磁序、缺陷或动力学指标的改进。若结果只在训练分布内有效，应通过跨温度、跨应变、跨缺陷浓度和跨超胞测试检查可迁移性。第一步可以选取团队已有的 HfO₂、二维磁体、半导体缺陷或钙钛矿数据做小样本试验，再决定是否扩大到生产级计算。

full_list.title_en: The Agentic AI Kerr Lab: LLM Agents for Kerr Microscopy Experiments with Magnetic Skyrmions
full_list.title_zh: Agentic AI Kerr实验室：用于磁性Skyrmions的Kerr显微镜实验的LLM代理
full_list.abstract: arXiv:2611.00299v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Magnetic skyrmions are topological spin textures that can be observed directly by magnetic microscopy and driven by fields and currents, which makes them a model system for fundamental physics and candidates for spintronic devices. Magneto-optical Kerr microscopy is a method to image them in real time; however, most experiments use an inefficient cycle of consecutive imaging, analysis and excitation in which every step requires the judgement of the experimentalist operating the setup. Here we present the Agentic AI Kerr Lab (AgentKerr), in which an agent based on a large language model operates this cycle automatically and efficiently on a Kerr microscope. Rather than relying on pattern detection by a language model, a convolutional neural network trained on Kerr images turns live images into skyrmion observables such as position, size and shape, on which the agent bases its decisions. The architecture lets agents operate the instruments safely, as every hardware action is checked deterministically against an action policy, independently of the agent that issues it. With no procedure given, the agent determines by itself how to create, tune and move skyrmions, and writes its own analyses. The approach can be transferred to other spin textures and points towards magnetic imaging experiments in which the researcher poses the question and the agent finds the way to realize the experiments that yield the answer.

full_list.title_en: Derivation of Novel Isotropic Metamaterials at the Hashin Shtrikman Stiffness Limit Enabled by Physics Informed Neural Networks
full_list.title_zh: 文献研究：Derivation of Novel Isotropic Metamaterials at the Hashin Shtrikman Stiffness Limit Enabled by Physics Informed Neural Networks
full_list.abstract: arXiv:2611.02622v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Current methods of deriving ultrastiff isotropic metamaterials require heuristics or topology optimization, which are highly inefficient and limited by human input. To circumvent this, Physics Informed Neural Networks are applied to analytical equations to systematically solve for plate orientations in closed cell lattices. Following a standardized procedure, the plate orientations were modelled and assembled into geometries resembling quasi random foams for validation via finite element simulations. Closed cell 6-plate geometries were also additively manufactured using LAPIS and experimentally characterized. The results indicate that a minimum of 6 plates is required to constitute an ultrastiff isotropic lattice, 7 plates would return the established plate Cubic Octet structure while 8 to 10 plate geometries did not show significant differences in properties. Despite the introduction of some plate bending due to sub-optimal plate placement strategy, relative stiffness of the PINNs lattices adheres closely to the Hashin Shtrikman upper bound, 90 percent of Hashin Shtrikman upper bound at a relative density of 0.4, and the lattices maintain near isotropic behaviour, achieving a Zener ratio of 0.95 at a relative density of 0.1. Benchmarking results show that specific stiffness of PINNs lattices is higher than the majority of isotropic architectures reported in the literature.

full_list.title_en: Site-orbit masked twin-branch Transformer for symmetry-constrained crystal generation
full_list.title_zh: 文献研究：Site-orbit masked twin-branch Transformer for symmetry-constrained crystal generation
full_list.abstract: arXiv:2611.02906v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Generative models for crystal structure prediction (CSP) have expanded the search space for novel materials and improved screening efficiency. However, simultaneously generating stable and novel structures remains challenging because of the complex structural and physical constraints governing crystals. To address this challenge, we propose site-orbit masked twin-branch Transformer model (ST2M), a symmetry-guided discrete--continuous diffusion framework incorporating degree-of-freedom masks and conditioned on Wyckoff patterns. ST2M represents crystal structures as sequences of independent occupied Wyckoff orbits and employs a twin-branch Transformer to jointly denoise discrete and continuous variables. In our experiments, ST2M achieves a structural validity of 96.37%. For known patterns in dataset, 23.86% of generated structures simultaneously satisfy stability, uniqueness, and novelty criteria, representing a relative improvement of 68.15% over the best-performing baseline. First-principles calculations identify a total of 21 previously unreported stable structures among selected candidates with low predicted energies. These results demonstrate that ST2M can generate chemically viable crystal candidates under prescribed crystallographic constraints and generalize to unknown Wyckoff patterns, providing a practical route to accelerated materials discovery.

full_list.title_en: Artificial Intelligence-Assisted Prediction and Optimization of Methylene Blue Adsorption onto Albizia lebbeck Bio-adsorbent Using Ensemble Machine Learning
full_list.title_zh: 文献研究：Artificial Intelligence-Assisted Prediction and Optimization of Methylene Blue Adsorption onto Albizia lebbeck Bio-adsorbent Using Ensemble Machine Learning
full_list.abstract: This study investigates the adsorption of methylene blue (MB)from aqueous solution using a bio-adsorbent prepared from Albizialebbeck pods and evaluates the predictive performance of ensemble machine learning models for modeling the adsorption process. The bio-adsorbent was characterized using pH PZC , Fourier Transform Infrared spectroscopy (FTIR), X-ray Diffraction (XRD),and Scanning Electron Microscopy with Energy Dispersive Spectroscopy (SEM–EDS). Characterization revealed a porous, carbon-rich, predominantly amorphous structure with abundant oxygen-containing functional groups favourable for dye adsorption. The effects of solution pH, contact time, adsorbent dosage, and initial dye concentration were systematically investigated through batch adsorption experiments. Equilibrium and kinetic data were analysed using Langmuir, Freundlich, and Temkin isotherm models, as well as pseudo-first-order, pseudo-second-order, and intraparticle diffusion kinetic models. The Langmuir isotherm provided the best equilibrium fit, yielding a maximum monolayer adsorptioncapacityof424.24mgg − 1 , while the pseudo-second-order model best described the adsorption kinetics. Furthermore, ensemble machine learning models—Random Forest (RF) and eXtreme Gradient Boosting(XGBoost)—were developed and optimized to predict adsorption performance. The optimized RF model achieved an R 2 value of 0.98876 for MB removal efficiency, while XGBoost attained an R 2 of0.99953 for adsorption capacity prediction. These findings demonstrate that Albizia lebbeck bio-adsorbent is a highly efficient, eco-friendly material for MB removal, and that ensemble learning provides a robust and accurate framework for predicting and optimizing adsorption processes in wastewater treatment.

full_list.title_en: TopoQuant: Topological Framework to Characterize Behavioral Shifts in Quantized Large Language Models
full_list.title_zh: 文献研究：TopoQuant: Topological Framework to Characterize Behavioral Shifts in Quantized Large Language Models
full_list.abstract: arXiv:2611.00631v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Post-training quantization (PTQ) reduces the com putational cost of large language models (LLMs), but it can introduce internal structural and behavioral changes that are not captured by traditional metrics such as accuracy and per plexity. We present TopoQuant, a topological framework that uses topological data analysis (TDA) to quantify structural drift in self-attention weights and relate it to behavioral changes in quantized LLMs. Across four LLM families and multiple quantization levels, we show that topological drift remains stable at moderate compression levels but increases sharply below 4 bit precision, closely tracking declines in attention agreement. Our results reveal a strong relationship between topological drift and attention agreement, indicating that structural changes in model parameters closely reflect behavioral degradation under quantization. We further demonstrate that topological features can accurately predict attention consistency using lightweight machine learning models, achieving R2 scores of up to 0.85. Predicting attention agreement enables efficient assessment of be havioral consistency in quantized LLMs, allowing quantization induced degradation to be detected without running expensive downstream tasks. The results indicate that topological drift pro vides an efficient early-warning signal for quantization-induced degradation and can help identify safe compression limits without extensive downstream evaluation.

full_list.title_en: Physics-informed X-ray tomography of magnetization and material parameters
full_list.title_zh: 文献研究：Physics-informed X-ray tomography of magnetization and material parameters
full_list.abstract: arXiv:2611.00528v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Three-dimensional spin textures are stabilized by microscopic interactions within their host materials. X-ray vector tomography can image these nanoscale structures, but weak magnetic contrast and a limited range of viewing angles often leave parts of the magnetization poorly determined. Here we show that a reconstruction constrained by the micromagnetic energy recovers the three-dimensional magnetization from such data and gains sensitivity to the underlying material interactions. Applied to the chiral magnet Co₈Zn₉Mn₃, the method resolves the three-dimensional helical texture even from a small fraction of the dual-axis projections typically required for a successful tomographic reconstruction, or from a single tilt axis alone. By testing which ratio of exchange to Dzyaloshinskii-Moriya interaction in the reconstruction best reproduces the measured projections, we obtain a value for the sample that differs by about 10 % from the literature value derived from the helical winding period. Taken together, our findings suggest a way to reduce the time needed for vector tomography and to extend it to determining fundamental magnetic interactions in a material.

full_list.title_en: Physics-Informed Surrogate for Sb2S3 Dispersion Trimming in Thin-Film Lithium Niobate
full_list.title_zh: 文献研究：Physics-Informed Surrogate for Sb2S3 Dispersion Trimming in Thin-Film Lithium Niobate
full_list.abstract: arXiv:2611.02652v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: A film-thickness error of 8 nm, within the tolerance of commercial thin-film lithium niobate wafers, shifts the group-velocity dispersion β₂ at 1550 nm by about 28 ps² km⁻¹. We study numerically whether a segmented, non-volatile phase-change cladding can correct this error after fabrication. In mode solves of 3012 geometries, Sb₂S₃ switches β₂ by a median of 181 ps² km⁻¹ at a 40 nm strip thickness with no material absorption under the adopted optical constants, whereas Sb₂Se₃ reaches a comparable contrast at a median modal loss of 5.6 dB cm⁻¹. Because phase adds along the guide, four independently switched binary segments reach a two-dimensional region of the (β₂,β₃) plane; eigenmode expansion supports this description at the junctions. Full-wave solves at 65 die geometries show that the segment states move with the die error, so the bit pattern is chosen from a per-die model: a spectral surrogate constrained by exact identities of the lossless Maxwell problem. Its accuracy within the training domain is similar to that of unconstrained baselines; it keeps β₂ and β₃ consistent, and its error at an unseen film thickness is 8.3 rather than 13.0 ps² km⁻¹. With a bare test ring and a second ring carrying a crystalline strip already on the mask, 96.8% of the dies are trimmed into ±25 ps² km⁻¹, scored on full-wave solutions. A thermal model gives a candidate write window for a 532 nm beam.

full_list.title_en: Atomistic Insights into MOCVD Growth of GaAs using a Closed Loop Autonomous System Combining Directed Reinforcement Learning and Kinetic Monte Carlo Simulations
full_list.title_zh: 文献研究：Atomistic Insights into MOCVD Growth of GaAs using a Closed Loop Autonomous System Combining Directed Reinforcement Learning and Kinetic Monte Carlo Simulations
full_list.abstract: arXiv:2611.01646v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Conventional process optimization of the Metal-Organic Chemical Vapor Deposition (MOCVD) growth parameters to achieve high-quality thin films relies on iterative, resource-intensive experimental runs. While predictive modeling can circumvent this cost and effort, simulating thin-film growth is constrained by the vastly different length and time scales of the deposition process. While continuum (e.g., Computational Fluid Dynamics (CFD)) and first-principles methods (e.g., Molecular Dynamics (MD)) struggle to balance experimental length/time scales and atomistic accuracy, Kinetic Monte Carlo (KMC) bridges this divide by resolving atomistic events whilst remaining tractable at experimental length and time scales. However, the accuracy of KMC relies on kinetic rate parameters that require costly density functional theory (DFT) calculations. In order to circumvent this, we present a framework that calibrates the rate parameters directly against experimental growth data. A forward KMC growth model is coupled in a closed loop with a Monte Carlo Tree Search (MCTS) optimizer that navigates the high-dimensional parameter space, with the search steered by the degree of rate control of each reaction rate parameter. The approach invokes no material-specific assumptions and hence, any deposition process whose forward kinetics can be reduced to a set of rate-controlled events is amenable to the same treatment. We demonstrate it for the MOCVD of GaAs, where the calibrated model captures the characteristic temperature dependence of the measured growth rate. The framework is also able to recover the three well known kinetic regimes characterized by change in the rate determining step from precursor chemisorption to desorption. As a result, the framework converts routinely measured growth data into a mechanistically interpretable model of the deposition process.

full_list.title_en: Neural network approximation of regularized density functionals
full_list.title_zh: 文献研究：Neural network approximation of regularized density functionals
full_list.abstract: arXiv:2511.18512v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We study neural-network approximation of density functionals in a Banach-space setting. Since the exact continuum functionals are discontinuous in the natural density topology, we apply p-Moreau-Yosida regularization. We construct finite-rank ReLU networks that preserve convexity and nonnegativity, lie below the regularized functional, and approximate it uniformly on compact sets. For energies obtained by minimization over compact density sets, we account exactly for the energy shift caused by regularization and bound the remaining error by the localization on these compact sets and network approximation errors. We apply this framework to canonical and grand-canonical density-functional theory at fixed particle number and fixed mean particle number, respectively. We obtain uniform energy convergence on norm-compact classes of external potentials, including molecular Coulomb potentials. We illustrate our results through numerical experiments on a simple model system.

full_list.title_en: Data-driven candidate structure ensemble generation beyond the convex hull with crystALL approach
full_list.title_zh: 文献研究：Data-driven candidate structure ensemble generation beyond the convex hull with crystALL approach
full_list.abstract: arXiv:2611.02584v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Real materials consist of multiple stable or metastable states under real-world conditions, existing as statistical ergodic ensembles of configurations rather than ideal crystals. Yet, data-driven computational materials discovery increasingly biases itself toward finding "new stable structures" from ground-state DFT calculations alone. This limits our long-term ability to discover materials whose properties emerge from metastable phases, to explain experimental observations, or to model thermodynamic behavior comprehensively. Predicting ergodic sets of atomic configurations of known and hypothetical solids is a fundamental challenge in theoretical crystallography, approached via many complementary methods. We discuss this conceptually and introduce crystALL, a pragmatic and powerful data-driven approach to discovering ensembles beyond the convex hull, embracing structural diversity over stability alone, enabling robust experiment matching in cases evading traditional methods. crystALL leverages 5 million relaxed structures from OPTIMADE and MPDD to rapidly generate a comprehensive candidate set by: (1) species substitutions; (2) ML feature-space analysis with pySIPFENN; (3) representative structure selection via clustering and energy-minimization or property matching; and (4) construction of the final candidate ensemble for experimental or ab initio validation. We also uniquely address the common challenge of experimental composition uncertainties spanning many integer stoichiometries by new efficient searches across anonymized compositional ranges rather than fixed formulas. Overall, crystALL's ensemble-focused philosophy provides critical advantages over the prevailing convex-hull-searching paradigm, which often fails to account for key experimental observations and increases AI/ML discovery bias over time - akin to model collapse in LLMs retrained on iteratively generated content.

full_list.title_en: Evidence-grounded large language models guide perovskite solar cell design and optimization
full_list.title_zh: 文献研究：Evidence-grounded large language models guide perovskite solar cell design and optimization
full_list.abstract: arXiv:2611.00633v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Using large language models to interpret experimental evidence, design discriminating experiments and formulate well-supported mechanistic explanations remains a central challenge in materials research. Here we establish PSM-Bench, an 800-question benchmark developed by perovskite researchers to evaluate scientific reasoning in perovskite photovoltaics. We also introduce OpenPerov, an expert-informed language-model framework that learns from expert-calibrated evidence records reconstructed from 4,532 articles; these records link experimental strategies, controls and observations to mechanistic interpretations. Structured-evidence adaptation outperformed conventional question-answer training, and OpenPerov Flash ranked first among 13 closed-book systems. OpenPerov Pro raised Scientific Mastery further, from 87.6 to 89.1, by revising selected passages with retrieved evidence. On questions derived from subsequent studies, both models also outscored expert-authored answers. In an experimental test of self-assembled monolayer design, OpenPerov selected a K analogue that outperformed the Na analogue preferred by experts. Devices incorporating the selected contact reached a power conversion efficiency of 27.05% and retained 96.74% of their steady-state reference efficiency after 1,000 h of dark thermal ageing at 85 ^circC. These results show that reconstructed scientific reasoning provides an effective basis for building domain models that interpret experiments and inform materials design.

full_list.title_en: Unified Learning of Interatomic Potentials and Electronic Hamiltonians, with Applications in 2D Materials
full_list.title_zh: 文献研究：Unified Learning of Interatomic Potentials and Electronic Hamiltonians, with Applications in 2D Materials
full_list.abstract: arXiv:2510.16605v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We introduce UnIPH, an equivariant graph neural network designed to jointly predict both interatomic potentials and tight-binding (TB) Hamiltonians for an atomic structure. UnIPH is trained using density functional theory (DFT) calculations followed by Wannier projection to predict energies and forces as node-level targets and Wannier-projected TB Hamiltonians as edge-level targets. This enables physically consistent modeling of coupled mechanical-electronic responses with near-DFT-level accuracy. After separately training two UnIPH models on DFT data for bilayer graphene and monolayer MoS2, respectively, we find that these models capture key deformation-electronic effects: in twisted bilayer graphene, the trained UnIPH reveals how interlayer spacing, in-plane strain, and out-of-plane corrugation drive isolated flat-band formation, and further shows that modulating substrate interaction strength can generate flat bands even away from the magic angle (approximately 1.1 degrees). For monolayer MoS2, UnIPH accurately reproduces phonon dispersions and strain-dependent band-gap evolution, and further predicts how a non-uniform substrate creates localized strain pockets that spatially modulate the conduction- and valence-band edges.

full_list.title_en: FACTO: fast atom-centered tensor operator for accurate and efficient foundational machine-learned interatomic potentials
full_list.title_zh: 文献研究：FACTO: fast atom-centered tensor operator for accurate and efficient foundational machine-learned interatomic potentials
full_list.abstract: arXiv:2611.03276v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: High-throughput inference remains a central challenge for equivariant machine-learned interatomic potentials. Here we introduce FACTO, an atom-centered equivariant architecture that confines evolving learned state and dense channel mixing to atoms, expressing neighbor interactions as fully fusible reductions. We complement this design with custom register-accumulated aggregation kernels and tensor-core FP32 emulation, accelerating inference while retaining FP32-level energy conservation under emulated arithmetic in molecular dynamics. Comprehensive evaluations on Matbench Discovery, MLIP Arena and MatCalc demonstrate high throughput alongside strong predictive accuracy and physical reliability. On Matbench Discovery, the four FACTO-OAM variants show top-tier performance by overall rank sum among 46 models with complete scores, advancing the accuracy-throughput Pareto frontier. On MLIP Arena, FACTO achieves state- of-the-art stability under extreme heating and compression, alongside high fidelity in hydrogen combustion. On MatCalc, FACTO outperforms the compared baselines in structural and elastic predictions while retaining competitive accuracy for energetic and thermal properties.

full_list.title_en: Machine Learning Aided Computational Discovery of Boride Substrates for Borophene Synthesis
full_list.title_zh: 文献研究：Machine Learning Aided Computational Discovery of Boride Substrates for Borophene Synthesis
full_list.abstract: arXiv:2611.00533v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Borophene, a monolayer of boron, is distinctive among two-dimensional materials owing to its unique properties, including polymorphism and potential applications in quantum technologies and energy conversion and storage. Nevertheless, its applications are hindered by the strong binding of borophene to metal substrates, which impedes the realization of freestanding borophene. Alternative substrates with tunable binding to borophene are therefore highly desirable. Since boride layers arise during borophene synthesis on metals, borides provide potential alternative substrates for borophene synthesis. In this work, we investigate the binding energies and interactions between borophene and 1356 boride surfaces for two borophene phases (v1/6 and v1/9), using density functional theory (DFT) calculations and machine learning (ML). Importantly, incorporating ML-predicted charge transfer as an input feature to a subsequent ML model enables physics-informed predictions of binding energies. Additional DFT calculations on four representative cases were performed to validate the ML predictions. SHAP analysis reveals that the majority of key descriptors are associated with delocalized electrons, highlighting the role of electronic properties in governing binding strength. Combined DFT and ML screening identifies 65 and 73 promising boride surfaces for the v1/6 and v1/9 phases, respectively. Al- and Ag-based borides, including AlB2 and AgB2, emerge as predominant candidates for both phases. The computationally predicted candidate substrates and the deduced design guidelines provide a charge-transfer-informed ML strategy for substrate selection and represent promising steps toward the experimental realization of freestanding borophene.

full_list.title_zh: 文献研究：PLUMED-JAX: GPU-native enhanced sampling for atomistic simulations
full_list.abstract: arXiv:2611.00483v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We present PLUMED-JAX, an AI-assisted adaptation of selected PLUMED collective variables, umbrella sampling, and metadynamics for JAX-based atomistic simulations, developed using gpt-6.1-sol with reasoning effort set to high within the Codex harness. Integration with JAX-MD supports compiled molecular dynamics, batched replicas, walkers sharing a bias, and execution across multiple graphics processing units. We validate the framework against PLUMED and exact free energy benchmarks, and demonstrate applications to butane, silicon crystallization, and lithium transport, with severalfold improvements in computational throughput for both classical forcefields and machine learning interatomic potentials.

full_list.title_en: Diffusion-Based Generative Screening of ABX₃ Perovskite Compositions for Bandgap-Targeted Materials Discovery
full_list.title_zh: 文献研究：Diffusion-Based Generative Screening of ABX₃ Perovskite Compositions for Bandgap-Targeted Materials Discovery
full_list.abstract: arXiv:2611.00766v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Crystal-generation models can explore compositions and atomic arrangements beyond a fixed set of crystal prototypes, but their usefulness for a specific materials family depends on whether the generated structures retain the defining topology and whether their predicted properties remain reliable across the sampled chemistry. Here, a pretrained diffusion model is used to generate candidate ABX₃ perovskites and to examine their structural, chemical and electronic-property distributions. A connectivity-based filter distinguishes three-dimensional corner-sharing perovskites from structures that share the same nominal ABX₃ stoichiometry. The accepted set contains substantial B-site multiplicity, including ordered double-perovskite configurations that are inaccessible to the two-prototype substitution reference used here. The generated set is enriched in chloride-, bromide- and iodide-containing compositions relative to the Materials Project, while all generated B-site elements are already represented in that database. On the downstream MP-trained ALIGNN scale, the predicted bandgap distribution is shifted towards 1.4 eV, but the target-window fraction (8.2%) is close to the MP reference fraction (7.3%); the separate MatterGen and ALIGNN label sources prevent this comparison from establishing target-condition enrichment. An ALIGNN model performs well on a formula-grouped random test split but does not outperform a constant baseline on a deliberately severe B-site-disjoint test. First-principles calculations on six generated structures show that relaxation can alter structural classification and that predicted and calculated gaps can differ appreciably. These results identify both the chemical-space coverage offered by crystal diffusion and the structural and predictive checks needed before its outputs can be treated as materials candidates.

full_list.title_en: Kernel Ridge Regression for conformer ensembles made easy with Structured Orthogonal Random Features
full_list.title_zh: 文献研究：Kernel Ridge Regression for conformer ensembles made easy with Structured Orthogonal Random Features
full_list.abstract: arXiv:2505.21247v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: A computationally efficient protocol for machine learning in chemical space using Boltzmann ensembles of conformers as input is proposed; the method is based on rewriting Kernel Ridge Regression expressions in terms of Structured Orthogonal Random Features, yielding physics-motivated trigonometric neural networks. To evaluate the method's utility for materials discovery, we test it on experimental datasets of two quantities related to battery electrolyte design, namely oxidation potentials in acetonitrile and hydration energies, using several geometry- and orbital-based molecular representations to demonstrate the method's flexibility. Despite only using computationally cheap force field calculations for conformer generation and generating orbital representations with GFN2-xTB calculations, we observe systematic decrease of prediction errors with increased training set size in all cases, with experimental accuracy reached after training on hundreds of molecules.

full_list.title_en: Optical Magnetic-Field Gating of Photon Avalanching Quantum Processes
full_list.title_zh: 文献研究：Optical Magnetic-Field Gating of Photon Avalanching Quantum Processes
full_list.abstract: arXiv:2611.01179v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Highly nonlinear phenomena, where macroscopic changes are triggered by microscopic perturbations, are ubiquitous in complex systems ranging from epidemic spreading to neural networks. In optics, photon avalanching represents a prime manifestation of such highly nonlinear behavior, characterized by a steep nonlinear response (s) following an avalanche threshold. However, this nonlinearity is typically determined by material composition, making this behavior challenging to tune for adaptive sensing, imaging, and neuromorphic applications. Here, we demonstrate giant optical magnetic field gated threshold and nonlinearity in lanthanide doped nanoparticles. We exploit the distinct quantum selection rules of the avalanche process: while the energy looping cycles of excited state absorption and cross relaxation are primarily electrically driven, the seed excitation, ground state absorption, is a mixed transition permitting magnetic dipole interaction. By positioning the emitters within an optical standing wave to spatially partition the electromagnetic field, we tune the local magnetic to electric field balance to selectively regulate the seeding and amplification probabilities. This allows us to demonstrate an unprecedented dynamic range of control over the power threshold and nonlinearity, tuning the order from s = 15 to s = 62. Furthermore, we harness this spatial separation of electric and magnetic fields using tightly focused cylindrical vector beams to locally sculpt the nonlinearity of a single nanocluster, achieving sub wavelength super resolution imaging that substantially surpasses conventional photon avalanche imaging under Gaussian illumination. These findings establish the magnetic component of light as a practical knob to actively program nonlinear optical dynamics, sub diffraction nanoscopy, and critical quantum dynamics at the nanoscale.

full_list.title_en: Learned Surrogates of Three-Dimensional Magnetohydrodynamic Turbulence
full_list.title_zh: 文献研究：Learned Surrogates of Three-Dimensional Magnetohydrodynamic Turbulence
full_list.abstract: arXiv:2611.01356v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Three-dimensional magnetohydrodynamic (MHD) turbulence, the flow of astrophysical and fusion plasmas, is costly to simulate. We present, to our knowledge, the first learned surrogates of three-dimensional resistive MHD turbulence, and compare three standard backbones in that role: a convolutional UNet, a shifted-window transformer and a Fourier neural operator. They are trained as autoregressive emulators of decaying MHD turbulence at a resolution of 128³ and Reynolds numbers of 1000, 3000 and 6000, on 500 simulations per Reynolds number, each with one two-stage procedure, single steps and then short rollouts, and stopped by one rule. Over a window of about one large-eddy turnover time, the UNet and the transformer reach relative velocity errors of 0.018 to 0.053 and keep the current sheets, the enstrophy, the current density and the energy spectra of the simulation; which of the two is the more accurate depends on the Reynolds number, the UNet leading at 3000 and 6000 and the transformer at 1000. Applied with the same backbones and training procedure to two public benchmarks, the models reach the lowest error reported to date on the isotropic turbulence set of FactFormer, 39% below the best published model. On the compressible MHD set of The Well, their rollout errors are a third to a half below those of the best of The Well's baselines. They also match a 1.3 B-parameter pretrained foundation model in its rollout windows, with 20-62 times fewer parameters. The code, the configuration of every model, the evaluation scripts and the data generator with the seed of every simulation will be released upon publication.

full_list.title_en: Structure of energy flux densities in Earth's magnetotail reconnection regions: Bridging simulation and observation
full_list.title_zh: 文献研究：Structure of energy flux densities in Earth's magnetotail reconnection regions: Bridging simulation and observation
full_list.abstract: arXiv:2611.02870v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Magnetic reconnection is important in both space and laboratory contexts because it changes the topology of magnetic fields and converts magnetic energy into particle energies. Establishing where this energy conversion occurs is critical for understanding how reconnection partitions energy. Using a novel machine learning approach based on simulations that explicitly identifies the separatrix regions for the first time, the partition of energy flux densities within the magnetic reconnection site is evaluated through statistical study of magnetotail reconnection events observed in situ. The separatrices are found to have the largest electron energy flux densities, roughly twice those in the exhaust, and Poynting flux densities about four times those in the inflows, whereas typical ion enthalpy flux densities are largest in the exhaust. The separatrices are therefore sites of intense electron and electromagnetic energy transport, although their small thickness means that the exhaust may still carry most of the total energy flux.

full_list.title_en: FlowBatt: Flow Matching for Probabilistic Battery Degradation Prediction
full_list.title_zh: 文献研究：FlowBatt: Flow Matching for Probabilistic Battery Degradation Prediction
full_list.abstract: arXiv:2611.03150v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Battery degradation remains a central challenge in the development and broad application of sustainable energy technologies. Accurate degradation prediction is challenging, as battery aging emerges from complex and heterogeneous interactions among cycling behavior, operating conditions, and cell chemistry. Existing machine-learning approaches typically focus on deterministic end-of-life predictions or modeling degradation curves within fixed chemistry settings, leaving probabilistic state of health (SOH) trajectory modeling across heterogeneous chemistries underexplored. We introduce FlowBatt, a use-inspired conditional generative framework that adapts flow matching with a diffusion transformer (DiT) backbone to battery degradation trajectory modeling. FlowBatt models full SOH trajectories as probabilistic degradation processes conditioned on early-cycle capacity data. To strengthen this conditioning pathway, we use explainable AI analysis to diagnose and improve the encoder that maps early-cycle capacity matrices into conditioning vectors. We evaluate FlowBatt on five public benchmark settings spanning diverse chemistries and aging conditions, comparing it with supervised and diffusion-based trajectory models as well as established baselines for remaining useful life (RUL) prediction under shared data splits. FlowBatt achieves the best trajectory-wise SOH prediction performance on all five datasets, with errors below 2.5%, and delivers competitive RUL prediction performance. By generating multiple plausible trajectories, FlowBatt provides empirical prediction intervals for battery degradation modeling. These results indicate that flow-matching-based trajectory modeling is a promising framework for probabilistic battery health prediction.

full_list.title_en: On-the-fly Δ-machine learned force fields for warm dense matter using a Yukawa reference model: Application to magnesium
full_list.title_zh: 使用Yukawa参考模型实时学习温暖致密物质的Δ-机器力场：应用于镁
full_list.abstract: arXiv:2611.00170v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We develop a framework for on-the-fly Δ-machine learned force field (Δ-MLFF) molecular dynamics (MD) simulations of warm dense matter (WDM). In particular, we employ a Yukawa reference model that captures the dominant screened-Coulomb interactions between the ions, with its parameters fit on the fly to Kohn--Sham density functional theory (DFT) data, and an MLFF scheme based on the kernel method and Bayesian linear regression that learns the differences in the energies, atomic forces, and stresses between the Yukawa model and Kohn--Sham DFT. We verify the accuracy and performance of the formalism by comparing the predicted properties of warm dense carbon with Kohn--Sham DFT results in the literature. In so doing, we demonstrate that Δ-MLFF has significantly lower errors in the energies, atomic forces, and stresses than the standard MLFF scheme at a comparable cost, while accelerating ab initio MD simulations by up to three orders of magnitude. We apply this framework to calculate the equation of state, structure, and transport properties of magnesium at densities of 5.22 to 10.44 g/cm³ and temperatures of 600 kK to 1.5 MK. We find that the pressure, self-diffusion coefficient, and shear viscosity obey power laws in temperature and density, that the dynamic structure factor exhibits a well-defined ion-acoustic mode whose negative dispersion is characteristic of strongly coupled liquids, and that the Stokes--Einstein relation holds to within 10% over the conditions considered.
full_list.abstract_zh: 我们开发了一个用于温密物质（ WDM ）的即时Δ机器学习力场（ Δ-MLFF ）分子动力学（ MD ）模拟的框架。特别是，我们使用Yukawa参考模型来捕获离子之间的主要屏蔽库仑相互作用，其参数即时拟合到Kohn-Sham密度泛函理论（ DFT ）数据，以及基于核方法和贝叶斯线性回归的MLFF方案，该方案学习Yukawa模型和Kohn-Sham DFT之间的能量、原子力和应力的差异。
full_list.abstract_zh_full: 我们开发了一个用于温密物质（ WDM ）的即时Δ机器学习力场（ Δ-MLFF ）分子动力学（ MD ）模拟的框架。特别是，我们使用Yukawa参考模型来捕获离子之间的主要屏蔽库仑相互作用，其参数即时拟合到Kohn-Sham密度泛函理论（ DFT ）数据，以及基于核方法和贝叶斯线性回归的MLFF方案，该方案学习Yukawa模型和Kohn-Sham DFT之间的能量、原子力和应力的差异。我们通过将暖致密碳的预测性质与文献中的Kohn-Sham DFT结果进行比较来验证形式化的准确性和性能。通过这样做，我们证明，与标准MLFF方案相比， Δ-MLFF在能量、原子力和应力方面的误差显著降低，成本相当，同时从头开始将MD模拟加速高达三个数量级。我们应用此框架计算密度为5.22至10.44 g/cm ³、温度为600 kK至1.5 MK时镁的状态、结构和输运特性方程。我们发现压力，自扩散系数和剪切粘度服从温度和密度的幂律，动态结构因子表现出明确的离子声模，其负色散是强耦合液体的特征，并且斯托克斯-爱因斯坦关系在考虑的条件下保持在10 ％以内。
full_list.summary: 我们开发了一个用于温密物质（ WDM ）的即时Δ机器学习力场（ Δ-MLFF ）分子动力学（ MD ）模拟的框架。特别是，我们使用Yukawa参考模型来捕获离子之间的主要屏蔽库仑相互作用，其参数即时拟合到Kohn-Sham密度泛函理论（ DFT ）数据，以及基于核方法和贝叶斯线性回归的MLFF方案，该方案学习Yukawa模型和Kohn-Sham DFT之间的能量、原子力和应力的差异。
full_list.method_point: 方法上，这篇工作可归入非绝热分子动力学、电子—声子耦合、Wannier/GW-BSE 和载流子输运。从摘要能确认的线索包括：分子动力学与有限温度轨迹, 密度泛函理论和电子结构计算，以及声子、有限温度和输运性质对应的结构或物理量。若迁移到团队流程，应采用“先用高精度电子结构和声子/电子—声子矩阵元建立小规模基准，再训练可迁移 Hamiltonian 或 ML 势，最后在长时间尺度非绝热 MD、输运或界面电荷转移中验证”的分层验证，而不是只比较单点能量或单一回归误差。还需核对原文的训练数据规模、损失函数、边界条件和误差分解，才能判断其是否适合团队的材料模拟任务。
full_list.related_work: 它与五位研究人员已有工作的直接连接是：非绝热分子动力学、电子—声子耦合、Wannier/GW-BSE 和载流子输运已经出现在团队的方向画像中，可对应到卤化物钙钛矿、二维半导体、FeSe、光电界面和能源材料。与传统只做 0 K formation energy/静态势垒的工作相比，这里更应关注声子、有限温度和输运性质在温度、缺陷、应变或外场下的变化；摘要没有给出的模型细节不作延伸判断。这种联系应通过同一材料体系上的独立基准和跨分布测试确认，不能仅凭方法名称或期刊来源下结论。
full_list.implication: 对当前研究最具体的启示不是泛泛地“使用 ML”，而是把该文的非绝热分子动力学、电子—声子耦合、Wannier/GW-BSE 和载流子输运嵌入现有材料模拟链：先在卤化物钙钛矿、二维半导体、FeSe、光电界面和能源材料中选择一个已有 DFT 数据基础的体系，按“先用高精度电子结构和声子/电子—声子矩阵元建立小规模基准，再训练可迁移 Hamiltonian 或 ML 势，最后在长时间尺度非绝热 MD、输运或界面电荷转移中验证”补充训练/验证集，再比较《使用Yukawa参考模型实时学习温暖致密物质的Δ-机器力场：应用于镁》对应模型对相稳定、极化/磁序、缺陷或动力学指标的改进。若结果只在训练分布内有效，应通过跨温度、跨应变、跨缺陷浓度和跨超胞测试检查可迁移性。第一步可以选取团队已有的 HfO₂、二维磁体、半导体缺陷或钙钛矿数据做小样本试验，再决定是否扩大到生产级计算。

full_list.title_en: Optimal Control of Chemical Reaction Networks with Thermodynamic Cost
full_list.title_zh: 文献研究：Optimal Control of Chemical Reaction Networks with Thermodynamic Cost
full_list.abstract: arXiv:2611.01734v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Thermodynamic control seeks to realize desired functions at minimal thermodynamic cost, yet existing frameworks remain largely confined to slow driving regimes or state-to-state transport. Here we establish a thermodynamic optimal-control theory for Markov jump processes (MJPs) and chemical reaction networks (CRNs) that accommodates objectives over both states and reaction fluxes beyond slow-driving limit. By deriving the thermodynamic Hamilton--Jacobi--Bellman equation, we demonstrate that the optimal dynamics take the form of a perturbed generalized-gradient flow driven by the value function. A convex representation of the entropy-production rate via generalized means identifies its Legendre--Fenchel dual as the dissipation function. The resulting dynamics shares the thermodynamic structure of CRNs and admits an information-geometric characterization. We further derive a thermodynamic Pontryagin equation by recasting the control problem in terms of thermodynamic forces, providing a complementary description of optimal trajectories and clarifying connections to thermodynamic optimal transport. Our results establish a thermodynamic and geometric foundation for controlling MJPs and CRNs beyond mere transport, opening avenues for optimizing biological processes and finite-time thermodynamic operations in far-from-equilibrium regimes.

full_list.title_en: Machine-Learned Interatomic Potential for the Mo-S-Al-O System
full_list.title_zh: 文献研究：Machine-Learned Interatomic Potential for the Mo-S-Al-O System
full_list.abstract: arXiv:2611.02403v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We develop a machine-learned neuroevolution potential (NEP) for the Mo-S-Al-O system, targeting MoS₂ heteroepitaxy on c-plane sapphire, α-Al₂O₃(0001). The potential is trained on 63,611 PBE+D3 structures distilled from about 1.1 million curated density-functional-theory (DFT) configurations, using an energy-difference loss function that directly targets interfacial and orientation-dependent energies. On held-out data, the energy and force errors are 29 meV/atom and 0.23 eV/mathringA. Validated against DFT on a suite of physical properties, the NEP reproduces the lattice constants within 0.3 %, the elastic constants within 17 %, the phonon dispersions with mean deviations below 2.5%, and the surface energies within 1.3 %. At the MoS₂/sapphire interface, it reproduces the adhesion energy minimum within 0.8 %, the interfacial energy within 2.2 % and the most stable orientation of the monolayer. It preserves the DFT-predicted energetic ordering of edges, point defects (Spearman ρ = 0.995) and mirror-twin boundaries (ρ = 1.0), and reproduces tilt grain-boundary energies within 8 % (ρ = 0.98) and stacking-fault energy barriers within 14 %. The resulting potential enables future studies of the atomic-scale mechanisms of defect formation in two-dimensional heteroepitaxy.

full_list.title_en: Unoccupied spin texture of ordered Bi films on vicinal Ge substrates
full_list.title_zh: 文献研究：Unoccupied spin texture of ordered Bi films on vicinal Ge substrates
full_list.abstract: arXiv:2611.02085v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Vicinal surfaces offer a compelling testing ground in surface science: breaking the high symmetry of a singular surface introduces periodic step arrays that can modify surface states on the terraces and influence epitaxial ordering; the interplay between these effects governs morphology and electronic structure, especially in heavy, spin--orbit-coupled materials. We combine low-energy electron diffraction (LEED) and spin-polarized inverse photoemission (SP-IPES) with ab-initio calculations for the Bi(1,1,1) reference, for the first time on a true high-index vicinal bismuth surface. On the ordered Bi(9,9,11) vicinal film selected by Ge(2,2,3), the measured unoccupied-state spin-sign sequence matches the calculated initial-state spectral function of Bi(1,1,1) terraces. Conversely, the pseudo-cubic Bi domains retained on Ge(4,4,3) and Ge(3,3,1) exhibit a characteristic spin-polarized surface-state response referenced to the macroscopic vicinal surface. These results show that the substrate cut selects not only the morphology of the Bi film, but also the crystallographic reference frame of its unoccupied spin texture.

full_list.title_en: Ab initio exploration of hydrogen-intercalated transition metal dichalcogenides: From identifying stable structures to emergent superconductivity
full_list.title_zh: 文献研究：Ab initio exploration of hydrogen-intercalated transition metal dichalcogenides: From identifying stable structures to emergent superconductivity
full_list.abstract: arXiv:2611.00271v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We present a first-principles study of hydrogen-intercalated transition metal dichalcogenides (TMDs), examining the structural, thermodynamic, electronic and superconducting properties of distinct intercalation configurations. In most configurations, the two intercalated hydrogen atoms contribute two electrons per unit cell, creating a band gap and thus rendering the system semiconducting. Among the dynamically stable configurations there is one exception to this rule, with inherently metallic behavior. The pristine phases of these materials are known to exhibit a charge density wave instability, which is fully suppressed by specific hydrogen configurations. Moreover, the semiconducting structures can be metallized by hole doping, albeit that the superconducting critical temperatures (T_c) are vanishingly low. On the other hand, electron doping drives the T_c up to 25 K, by populating dense states above the gap. This finding can motivate further experimental exploration of superconductivity in hydrogen-intercalated TMDs through ionic-liquid gating or alkali co-intercalation.

full_list.title_en: Density functionals for the Pauli-Fierz Hamiltonian
full_list.title_zh: 文献研究：Density functionals for the Pauli-Fierz Hamiltonian
full_list.abstract: arXiv:2611.01208v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We develop a density-functional theory for the Pauli-Fierz Hamiltonian of nonrelativistic quantum electrodynamics in the spirit of the convex-analytic formulation of Lieb. We consider finitely many electrons, subject to external scalar and vector potentials, coupled to the full continuum of massless transverse photons with an ultraviolet cutoff. The natural basic variables are the standard electron density and a combined current density, the sum of the paramagnetic current density and a field-induced current density generated by the quantized vector potential. We prove representability results for these density-current pairs and show that the mixed-state constrained-search functional attains its infimum and coincides with the Lieb functional obtained by convex conjugation. Since arbitrarily soft photons purify mixed states at a negligible energy cost without changing their density and combined current density, the pure-state Levy-Lieb functional equals the Lieb functional and is therefore convex, even though its infimum need not be attained. In addition, we establish the zero-coupling limit, which recovers the mixed-state Vignale-Rasolt functional of current-density-functional theory. Finally, we consider the long-wavelength (dipole) limit and show that the limiting functional can be written as a constrained search for the well-known length-gauge dipole Hamiltonian.

full_list.title_en: Evidence for topological flat band magnetism in Co₃Sn₂S₂
full_list.title_zh: 文献研究：Evidence for topological flat band magnetism in Co₃Sn₂S₂
full_list.abstract: arXiv:2611.00310v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Correlations and topology are central pillars in the study of emergent electronic phases. Topological flat bands near the Fermi level unite these concepts, providing a route towards correlated topological phenomena and unconventional magnetism. Despite theoretical predictions, momentum-resolved observation of a topological flat band at the Fermi level has remained elusive. Using angle resolved photoemission spectroscopy, we observe a flat band at the Fermi level within the topologically non-trivial electronic structure of the magnetic kagome Weyl semimetal Co₃Sn₂S₂. We further uncover a strong temperature dependence in which the flat band shifts across the Fermi level, accompanied by a reconstruction of the Fermi surface. Strikingly, this evolution occurs on the same temperature scale as previously reported anomalies in the magnetic response. Together, these results provide evidence for topological flat band magnetism in Co₃Sn₂S₂, establishing a microscopic setting in which topology, electronic correlations, and magnetism become intertwined.

full_list.title_en: Fractional quantum Hall effect at ν=1/2 in wide GaAs quantum wells: Subband structure, exact diagonalization, and the magnitude of the gap
full_list.title_zh: 文献研究：Fractional quantum Hall effect at ν=1/2 in wide GaAs quantum wells: Subband structure, exact diagonalization, and the magnitude of the gap
full_list.abstract: arXiv:2611.01885v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Recent experiments on a wide GaAs quantum well report a fractional quantum Hall state at filling factor ν=1/2 with an unusually large activation gap, a sharp maximum of the gap as a function of density, and a possible transition from the non-Abelian Moore-Read Pfaffian to the Abelian Halperin 331 state. We analyze this system theoretically, with self-consistent subband calculations, exact diagonalization, and a reanalysis of the published transport data. We find that the well has two relevant subbands, that with the second subband frozen out the well most likely has no incompressible state at ν=1/2, that a strict bilayer at the maxima of the charge density does not produce 331, and that an active second subband is essential: the ground state is a paired state of electrons in both subbands, on a continuous path between the Pfaffian and 331, with a neutral gap much larger than that of a one-subband Pfaffian. The position of the state on this path is controlled by electrostatic energies that the accessible system sizes contain only in part, and the standard overlaps do not identify the state at these sizes. Our results are more consistent with a Pfaffian-like state than with 331, but they are not definitive. The transport data do not support the reported magnitude of the gap; the gap we extract is smaller and comparable to the calculated two-subband neutral gap. A benchmark calculation for the Laughlin state at ν=1/3 in the same well provides an experimental test of the electrostatic treatment.

full_list.title_en: Many-Body Correlations in Phase-Space Microscopes
full_list.title_zh: 文献研究：Many-Body Correlations in Phase-Space Microscopes
full_list.abstract: arXiv:2611.03112v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The recently proposed "phase-space microscope" (PSM) extends quantum gas microscopes by allowing joint, single-shot measurements of position and momentum. We show that the n-body correlation functions constructed from such phase-space snapshots determine, in principle, all n-body observables of a many-body quantum state. This establishes phase-space imaging as a complete probe of strongly correlated matter, beyond what snapshots of position and momentum can provide---a limitation that goes back to a famous question posed by Pauli. Even without the full reconstruction of the density matrices, the PSM provides valuable insight into the quantum states. We demonstrate this power through several applications: witnessing entanglement hidden from both position and momentum, including between spatially separated collective degrees of freedom; resolving pairing structure across the BEC-BCS crossover, including the phase of the pair wavefunction and the reconstruction of its two-body Wigner function; probing inhomogeneous systems and preformed pairs without long-range order, relevant to the pseudogap phase; extracting the interaction energy in a magnetic field; and measurements of the local Chern marker. Furthermore, we discuss phase imprinting in the matter-wave Fourier plane as an alternative method for probing time-reversal-symmetry-broken phases such as chiral p-wave superconductors. Together, these results establish the PSM as a versatile new tool for exploring fundamental features of quantum many-body phases in strongly correlated quantum matter.

full_list.title_en: Superconductivity of bilayer two-orbital Hubbard model for La₃Ni₂O₇ under high pressure
full_list.title_zh: 文献研究：Superconductivity of bilayer two-orbital Hubbard model for La₃Ni₂O₇ under high pressure
full_list.abstract: arXiv:2511.01801v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: By combining density functional theory (DFT) and density matrix renormalization group calculations, we investigate the unusual pressure dependence of superconducting transition temperature (T_c) in the nickelate superconductor La₃Ni₂O₇. Using the hopping integrals and on-site potentials obtained by fitting the DFT band structures, we map a quantum phase diagram of a bilayer two-orbital Hubbard model with increasing pressure in a ladder geometry, which has an intermediate Hubbard repulsion and a Hund's coupling. Near 3/8 filling, we find a strong spin density wave order, which at 3/8 filling shows a real-space spin pattern similar to the spin-charge stripe order along a lattice direction. At 21/64 filling, we find a superconducting phase with interlayer superconductivity (SC) in both the dz^₂ and dₓ^₂₋y^₂ orbitals, as well as in-plane SC in the dz^₂ orbital. Intriguingly, the SC is weakened with increasing pressure and transits to a Luttinger liquid above 80 GPa, which qualitatively agrees with the experimental observations of decreasing T_c with increasing pressure and a transition to Fermi liquid above 80 GPa in La₃Ni₂O₇. Through a comparative study, we further show that the ratio of interaction to hopping integral, which reduces moderately with increasing pressure, may play a dominant role in the weakening of SC. Our results of this experimentally relevant model not only find a robust SC through suppressing the competing spin density wave order, but also give new insight into the unusual pressure dependence of SC in La₃Ni₂O₇.

full_list.abstract: arXiv:2611.00204v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Two wavefunctions have previously been proposed to describe the ν=1/2+1/2 quantum Hall bilayer: p-wave pairing of composite fermions and s-wave pairing of composite fermions with anti-composite fermions. We show analytically in the spherical geometry and within the Jain-Kamilla lowest Landau level projection scheme that both of these paired composite fermion wavefunctions exactly reproduce the Halperin (111) state for a specific form of the pairing that we derive. We also find a second wavefunction that is common between both classes of wavefunctions. However, we provide evidence the two variational families generate overlapping but not identical sets of electronic states, ruling out a universal reparametrization that identifies their wavefunctions.

full_list.title_en: Phase-Tunable Liouvillian Topology: Dual Winding Structures and Skin Effects
full_list.title_zh: 文献研究：Phase-Tunable Liouvillian Topology: Dual Winding Structures and Skin Effects
full_list.abstract: arXiv:2611.01110v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Liouvillian skin effects are usually associated with dissipation whose rates favor unidirectional flow. In this work, we show that directional edge localization can emerge even when population exchange between sites is exactly balanced, with a single tunable phase parameter α deciding their direction and a dual winding structure deciding their nature. Although this number-conserving bath is known for eigenstate selection, we demonstrate here that its phase controls a steady current, which Hamiltonian hopping converts to directional edge localization. Further, we study the spectral winding structure by independently twisting the left (ket) and right (bra) vector indices of the density matrix, revealing two distinct windings whose relationship is dictated by an antiunitary mirror symmetry. Nearest-neighbor jump operators break this symmetry: both windings coincide, giving rise to a common spectral winding W₀(α)=±1, producing a unipolar skin effect in which the density accumulates at a specific edge. However, next nearest neighbor jump preserve it. The two windings are forced to be opposite, and the ket and bra are pushed to opposite edges, giving a bipolar skin effect of coherences present in eigenmodes, without edge localization of the density in the steady state. Remarkably, in a dimerized chain the phase-controlled density skin effect gives the steady-state zero modes a size-independent weight at the skin edge, accompanied by a kink at the topological transition. In addition, the relaxation time grows linearly with the system size, however at specific phases α where the jump operators are rendered Hermitian, edge-localized eigenmodes with skin character coexist with diffusive relaxation.

full_list.abstract: arXiv:2611.02961v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The simultaneous suppression of lattice heat transport and enhancement of carrier transport is central to the development of high-performance thermoelectric materials. Here, we investigate the microscopic mechanisms governing phonon and carrier transport in CaAl₂Si₂-type AMg₂X₂ (A = Ca, Sr, Ba; X = P, As, Sb, Bi) Zintl compounds using first-principles calculations, machine-learning interatomic potentials, and Boltzmann transport theory. As X changes from P to Bi, the widening phonon band gap restricts three-phonon scattering channels and increases the relative importance of four-phonon processes. In CaMg₂Bi₂ and BaMg₂Bi₂, four-phonon scattering dominates the relaxation of low-frequency heat-carrying modes at 900 K. The Bi-based series also exhibits an anomalous increase in lattice thermal conductivity from Ca to Ba despite the increasing cation mass. Mode-resolved analysis links the lower thermal conductivity of CaMg₂Bi₂ to reduced low-frequency group velocities and stronger anharmonic scattering, with Ca-related mid-frequency vibrations providing additional four-phonon scattering channels. Including both particle-like and coherent contributions, its lattice thermal conductivity reaches 0.23 W·m⁻¹K⁻¹ at 900 K. Meanwhile, the increasing covalent character of the vertical Mg-X bonds is accompanied by enhanced band-edge dispersion and reduced carrier effective masses. These electronic changes, together with conduction-band convergence, favor n-type transport and yield a predicted peak ZT of 3.68 at 900 K in CaMg₂Bi₂. These results elucidate the interplay of phonon spectral structure and higher-order anharmonicity in thermal transport, alongside the distinct electronic response to anion substitution.

full_list.abstract: arXiv:2611.03423v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Propagating spin waves have emerged as promising candidates for signal processing and information transmission. We present a theoretical investigation of the generation, propagation and collection of spin-wave wave packets in micrometer-wide magnetic conduits, highlighting their potential for analogue frequency demultiplexing in space and time. We clarify the roles of the excitation duration and of the spin wave dispersion relation, as well as the influence of the spin-wave linewidth in setting the spatio-temporal evolution of propagating spin-wave wavepackets excited by Gaussian field pulses. We issue rules for the spatio-temporal separation of wavepackets that carry different frequencies. We finally propose an amplitude-conserving frequency demultiplexer based on a spin wave delay line of 60x5 μm² footprint.

full_list.title_zh: 文献研究：Band Alignment of Grafted versus Directly Bonded Si/Ge Heterostructures
full_list.abstract: arXiv:2611.02259v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The electronic properties of semiconductor heterostructures are influenced by the local bonding and electrostatic environment at the heterointerface. Here, we investigate how the interface-formation mechanism modifies the band alignment of Si/Ge heterostructures by directly comparing Al2O3-mediated semiconductor grafting with direct bonding. Interface-sensitive X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy combined with Kraut analysis reveals type-I band alignment for both structures, but with different band offsets: the valence-band offset increases from ~0.08 eV for directly bonded Si/Ge to ~0.21 eV for grafted Si/Al2O3/Ge, accompanied by a corresponding reduction in the conduction-band offset. Raman spectroscopy further distinguishes the two interfacial configurations. The different core-level shifts and band offsets indicate that the electronic structure is sensitive to the interfacial bonding and electrostatic environment introduced by the two integration schemes. These results demonstrate that, even for an identical Si/Ge material pair, the interface-formation pathway provides an additional degree of freedom for controlling heterojunction band alignment, offering a route toward interface-engineered electronic and optoelectronic devices.

full_list.title_zh: 文献研究：Cage-enforced i-wave altermagnetism in boron-carbon clathrates
full_list.abstract: arXiv:2611.03492v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The spin splitting of an altermagnet arises from a rotation that relates its two magnetic sublattices. In known cases it is fixed by the crystal structure. Here we show that guest-host frameworks separate the two roles. In the boron-carbon clathrates MB₃C₃ the ordered cage removes the translation between the two guest sites and enforces cubic i-wave altermagnetism, with six symmetry-enforced nodal planes, for any magnetic guest in the compensated state; strain retunes the class to d- or g-wave. We demonstrate the platform with GdB₃C₃: its compensated antiferromagnetic ground state is a narrow-gap semiconductor with spin splitting of 0.19 eV at the conduction-band edge, and its weakly pinned Néel vector switches the helicity-resolved optical response on and off according to the magnetic point group. Thermodynamic stability at high pressure and dynamical stability at ambient pressure indicate that it can be made by the route established for this family.

full_list.title_en: Defect Chemistry of Hafnia-Based Ferroelectrics under Oxide-Electrode Constraints
full_list.title_zh: 文献研究：Defect Chemistry of Hafnia-Based Ferroelectrics under Oxide-Electrode Constraints
full_list.abstract: arXiv:2611.02317v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: HfO₂ heterostructures with La₀.₆₇Sr₀.₃₃MnO₃ (LSMO) epitaxial electrodes have attracted interest as ferroelectric systems with electrode-dependent defect chemistry. However, the formation and stability of defects under LSMO-constrained chemical conditions remain poorly understood. In this work, we use density functional theory calculations to systematically investigate oxygen vacancies and La-, Sr-, and Mn-related interstitial and substitutional defects in HfO₂ under chemical environments constrained by the LSMO electrode. We find that LSMO stability substantially narrows the accessible O chemical potential range relative to bulk HfO₂, altering the predicted defect formation energies. While La and Sr substitutional defects are governed primarily by preferred ionic valence states, oxygen vacancies and Mn substitutional defects exhibit charge states sensitive to the local atomic environment. In addition, defect-complex calculations in orthorhombic HfO₂ reveal negative binding energies, indicating favorable defect association. The La- and Mn-related defect complexes exhibit thermodynamic competition, with their relative stability depending on the Fermi level and oxygen chemical potential. Lastly, extending the analysis to Hf₀.₅Zr₀.₅O₂ and ZrO₂ reveals common oxygen-vacancy trends, while the stability of LSMO-derived defects depends more strongly on the host material and crystal phase. These results provide a thermodynamic basis for understanding how electrode-constrained chemical environments and host structures influence defect formation, charge compensation, and defect-complex stability in HfO₂-based materials.

full_list.abstract: arXiv:2601.07098v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: The electric field gradients (EFGs) at the (non-spherical) nucleus contribute to atomic and molecular hyperfine structure and govern Nuclear Electric field gradients (EFGs) at nuclei contribute to atomic hyperfine structure and govern Nuclear Quadrupole Resonance (NQR) and Mössbauer spectroscopy, providing a sensitive probe of local electronic structure and symmetry. EFGs can be obtained from electronic-structure calculations and inferred from spectroscopic measurements, linking theory and experiment. In this work, we use representative molecular and crystalline examples to examine selected factors that control calculated EFGs, with particular emphasis on multiconfigurational embedded-cluster calculations for solids. We analyze the sensitivity of EFGs to geometry and to computational choices including basis set, correlation treatment, and active-space construction. We also discuss differences in EFG tensor conventions adopted by commonly used quantum-chemistry codes and their implications for comparing computational results. Periodic calculations are used where appropriate as reference data for assessing the embedded-cluster description. Our results provide practical guidelines for the reliable computation and interpretation of EFGs as descriptors of the electronic structure and local chemical environment.

full_list.title_en: Establishing Néel order in the square-lattice antiferromagnetic Heisenberg model: a bootstrap proof
full_list.title_zh: 文献研究：Establishing Néel order in the square-lattice antiferromagnetic Heisenberg model: a bootstrap proof
full_list.abstract: arXiv:2611.03241v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Rigorously establishing spontaneous symmetry breaking (SSB) in the thermodynamic limit is generally challenging. This is exemplified by the two-dimensional (2D) S = 1/2 antiferromagnetic Heisenberg model where the existence of Néel order is not rigorously established despite overwhelming evidence from a variety of methods. We show that a bootstrap approach can be used to rigorously establish SSB and use it to prove the existence of Néel order in the 2D S = 1/2 XXZ model by deriving a strictly positive lower bound on the Néel order parameter for a set of discrete values of the anisotropy parameter Δ in the range [0,2] including the isotropic (Heisenberg) point Δ = 1. Our approach employs a generalization of the Kennedy--Lieb--Shastry inequalities, which use an infrared bound to reduce the existence of long-range order to bounds on certain finite-distance correlators. We compute these bounds for all sufficiently large systems with periodic boundary conditions using the bootstrap. An important ingredient in our proof is a novel method for obtaining exactly certified variational upper bounds on the energy density in the thermodynamic limit from matrix product states. Our approach can be readily generalized to other local lattice models for which infrared susceptibility bounds can be obtained.

full_list.title_en: Fabry-Pérot Cavity formed by Magnonic waveguide using holes and notches
full_list.title_zh: 由磁波导使用孔和凹口形成的法布里-佩罗腔
full_list.abstract: arXiv:2611.00178v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In this paper, we have investigated a spin-wave-based Fabry-Pérot (FP) cavity using two air holes and notches embedded in a magnonic waveguide. Through micromagnetic simulations, we have demonstrated the spin-wave profile, as well as the transmission and reflection spectra of the FP type magnonic waveguide, by varying the distance between the center of holes and notches. We have introduced an analysis of the reflection spectra in an FP type magnonic waveguide, which is essential and considerable for the performance of magnonic integrated circuits. We have also presented a theoretical model to describe the transmission and reflection characteristics of the FP-type magnonic waveguide. Furthermore, active tuning of the resonance peak of the FP type magnonic wavguide by varying the external magnetic field has been demonstrated. Our proposed structure and its study may contribute to the development of magnonic integrated circuits for low-power computing and data processing in next-generation spintronic technologies.
full_list.abstract_zh: 在本文中，我们使用嵌入在磁波导中的两个气孔和凹口研究了基于自旋波的法布里-佩罗（ FP ）腔。通过微磁模拟，我们通过改变孔和凹口中心之间的距离，演示了FP型磁波导的自旋波剖面以及透射和反射光谱。我们引入了FP型磁波导中反射光谱的分析，这对于磁集成电路的性能至关重要。我们还提出了一个理论模型来描述FP型磁波导的透射和反射特性。此外，还演示了通过改变外部磁场来主动调谐FP型磁波导的谐振峰。
full_list.abstract_zh_full: 在本文中，我们使用嵌入在磁波导中的两个气孔和凹口研究了基于自旋波的法布里-佩罗（ FP ）腔。通过微磁模拟，我们通过改变孔和凹口中心之间的距离，演示了FP型磁波导的自旋波剖面以及透射和反射光谱。我们引入了FP型磁波导中反射光谱的分析，这对于磁集成电路的性能至关重要。我们还提出了一个理论模型来描述FP型磁波导的透射和反射特性。此外，还演示了通过改变外部磁场来主动调谐FP型磁波导的谐振峰。我们提出的结构及其研究可能有助于下一代自旋电子技术中用于低功耗计算和数据处理的磁性集成电路的发展。

full_list.method_point: 方法上，这篇工作可归入磁性机器学习势、自旋 Hamiltonian、自旋—晶格动力学和非共线磁结构。从摘要能确认的线索包括：论文题目和摘要中可确认的方法，以及磁性、自旋以及自旋—晶格耦合对应的结构或物理量。若迁移到团队流程，应采用“训练集同时覆盖原子位移和自旋构型，显式标注交换、各向异性、DMI 或自旋力；用自旋 MD/MC 与 DFT 自旋能差验证温度、应变和缺陷下的磁序稳定性”的分层验证，而不是只比较单点能量或单一回归误差。还需核对原文的训练数据规模、损失函数、边界条件和误差分解，才能判断其是否适合团队的材料模拟任务。
full_list.related_work: 它与五位研究人员已有工作的直接连接是：磁性机器学习势、自旋 Hamiltonian、自旋—晶格动力学和非共线磁结构已经出现在团队的方向画像中，可对应到CrI₃/CrSBr 等范德华磁体、反铁磁/交替磁材料、磁性氧化物。与传统只做 0 K formation energy/静态势垒的工作相比，这里更应关注磁性、自旋以及自旋—晶格耦合在温度、缺陷、应变或外场下的变化；摘要没有给出的模型细节不作延伸判断。这种联系应通过同一材料体系上的独立基准和跨分布测试确认，不能仅凭方法名称或期刊来源下结论。
full_list.implication: 对当前研究最具体的启示不是泛泛地“使用 ML”，而是把该文的磁性机器学习势、自旋 Hamiltonian、自旋—晶格动力学和非共线磁结构嵌入现有材料模拟链：先在CrI₃/CrSBr 等范德华磁体、反铁磁/交替磁材料、磁性氧化物中选择一个已有 DFT 数据基础的体系，按“训练集同时覆盖原子位移和自旋构型，显式标注交换、各向异性、DMI 或自旋力；用自旋 MD/MC 与 DFT 自旋能差验证温度、应变和缺陷下的磁序稳定性”补充训练/验证集，再比较《由磁波导使用孔和凹口形成的法布里-佩罗腔》对应模型对相稳定、极化/磁序、缺陷或动力学指标的改进。若结果只在训练分布内有效，应通过跨温度、跨应变、跨缺陷浓度和跨超胞测试检查可迁移性。第一步可以选取团队已有的 HfO₂、二维磁体、半导体缺陷或钙钛矿数据做小样本试验，再决定是否扩大到生产级计算。

full_list.title_en: Fermi surface and field-induced Lifshitz transition in the antiferromagnet NbMnP exhibiting an anomalous Hall effect
full_list.title_zh: 文献研究：Fermi surface and field-induced Lifshitz transition in the antiferromagnet NbMnP exhibiting an anomalous Hall effect
full_list.abstract: arXiv:2611.02360v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We performed Shubnikov--de Haas (SdH) oscillation measurements on the Q=0 antiferromagnet NbMnP, which exhibits a large anomalous Hall effect. The SdH frequencies observed in the low-field region up to 17.5~T are well described by first-principles band-structure calculations based on the B₃g+B₂ᵤ noncollinear magnetic structure determined by neutron diffraction. The effective masses are enhanced by approximately a factor of two relative to the calculated band masses. High-field measurements up to 41.5~T reveal a Lifshitz transition accompanied by a pronounced evolution of the SdH frequency spectrum. These results confirm that first-principles calculations provide a reliable tool for the development of functional antiferromagnetic materials, while also demonstrating that field-induced changes in the Fermi surface itself need to be taken into account in understanding their high-field magnetotransport properties.
